info.title: pgproj
info.description: PostgreSQL database project compiler: builds a schema from SQL files, compares it with a live database, and publishes the difference.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
PostgreSQL Database Project compiler.

Parses the SQL files referenced by a pgproj.json project, builds a semantic model of the database schema, and can compare or publish that model against a live PostgreSQL database.

Examples:
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app"
  pgproj build
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app"
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute
  pgproj document --format html,markdown,json
  pgproj about

commands.name: init
commands.description:
Connects to a live PostgreSQL database, reads its schema, and writes a new pgproj project from it: a generated pgproj.json and one SQL file per object.

Where each object is written:
  - One file per table, view, function, procedure, sequence, type, aggregate, operator, collation, text search dictionary and configuration, cast, event trigger, and publication.
  - A table's constraints, indexes, triggers, row-level security policies, rules, extended statistics, and grants live alongside it, in the table's file. A materialized view's indexes live in the view's file.
  - Schema-level and default-privilege grants, and a schema's comment, live in the schema's own file.
  - An object's owner and comment live beside the object; a constraint's, trigger's, or policy's comment follows it.

Refuses to overwrite an existing pgproj.json or write into a non-empty output directory unless --force is given.

When a function body or a type names another function or type without a schema, because the database found it through the search_path of the session that created it, the generated pgproj.json sets "searchPath" to the fewest schemas that find them all, followed by public, so the project builds. init says so when it does.

The generated pgproj.json's sourceConnectionString is --source-connection as given, with the password replaced by a placeholder; it records where the project came from, and document --source-connection with no value reads it. It is never the database diff and publish change: name that with --target-connection, the PGPROJ_TARGET_CONNECTION environment variable, or targetConnectionString, which init does not write.

Not read by pgproj, so absent from the scaffolded project even if the database has them:
  - roles and their settings (role memberships are scaffolded)
  - text search parsers and templates (a text search configuration and a dictionary are scaffolded)
  - tablespaces (a table's TABLESPACE clause is scaffolded)
  - foreign data wrappers, servers, user mappings, and foreign tables
  - subscriptions
  - operator classes and families
  - conversions
  - base types (CREATE TYPE with INPUT and OUTPUT functions), with their input and output functions
  - languages
  - transforms
  - access methods
  - security labels
  - database-level settings
  - comments on event triggers, rules, operators, aggregates, casts, publications, and a domain's constraints (the objects themselves are scaffolded)
  - indexes PostgreSQL marks INVALID, left by a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (each is named)
Check for them before relying on the scaffold as complete.

Choosing what is scaffolded:
  - --schemas scaffolds only the schemas listed; --exclude-schemas scaffolds all but the schemas listed (not both). The generated pgproj.json lists the schemas that were modeled.
  - --exclude-grants/--exclude-role-memberships/--exclude-owners skip scaffolding that category, and are also written into the generated pgproj.json so later build/diff/publish runs keep matching.

A database with a schema per tenant (--tenant-prefix tenant, where the tenants are tenant_acme, tenant_globex, ...):
  - The shared schemas are scaffolded as usual; the tenants' are not.
  - One tenant (the first by name, or --tenant-from acme) is scaffolded into the Tenant folder of --output, with its schema name taken out, so it reads as the template every tenant is built from. Where it names the schema itself (GRANT ... ON SCHEMA), it names the prefix, the template's stand-in schema.
  - The other tenants are compared with the template, and each that differs is named; pgproj diff shows how.
  - pgproj.json gets a "tenants" block: the template folder and the prefix, and, with --tenant-file, tenants.csv listing the tenants found, or, with --tenant-query, the query that lists them. See docs/notes/tenants.md.

Other files:
  - --report writes a Markdown report of the run at the root of --output.
  - --erd writes a Mermaid entity relationship diagram of the scaffolded tables (erd-<time>.mmd in the directory of pgproj.json, or the path given), built from the new SQL files; the report links it.
  - --erd-schemas/--erd-exclude-schemas narrow the diagram to some schemas.
  - --erd-html also writes a web page that draws the diagram in a browser (it loads Mermaid from a CDN).
  - --erd-existing overwrite|backup|keep says what to do with a file already at the path (the default backs up a file --erd wrote and keeps any other).

--verbose also writes each step, its time, and each file written to standard error. --quiet writes nothing but errors (including the notice above, so check it before relying on the scaffold).

Examples:
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=postgres"
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" -o ./schema --project ./db/pgproj.json
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --force
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --exclude-grants --exclude-role-memberships
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --schemas app,reporting --report
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --exclude-schemas audit,staging
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --report --erd
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --verbose
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --tenant-prefix tenant
  pgproj init --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --tenant-prefix tenant --tenant-from acme --tenant-file

options.name: --project
options.description: Path to write the new pgproj.json file to. Defaults to 'pgproj.json' in the current directory. [default: pgproj.json]

options.name: --source-connection
options.description: PostgreSQL connection string of the database to read the schema from (the source). If not given, the PGPROJ_SOURCE_CONNECTION environment variable is used; one of them is required.

options.name: --output
options.description: Base directory to write the scaffolded SQL files to, relative to --project's directory unless absolute. Created (including any missing parent directories) if it doesn't already exist. Defaults to './sql'. [default: ./sql]

options.name: --name
options.description: Name for the generated pgproj.json's "name" field. Defaults to the database name from --source-connection.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite an existing pgproj.json at --project or write into a non-empty --output directory. Without this, init refuses to touch either. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude-grants
options.description: Don't scaffold object/schema/column privilege grants. When given, the generated pgproj.json also sets excludeGrants: true, so later build/diff/publish runs keep matching what was scaffolded. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude-role-memberships
options.description: Don't scaffold role memberships (GRANT role TO grantee). When given, the generated pgproj.json also sets excludeRoleMemberships: true, so later build/diff/publish runs keep matching what was scaffolded. [default: False]

options.name: --exclude-owners
options.description: Don't scaffold object owners (ALTER ... OWNER TO). When given, the generated pgproj.json also sets excludeOwners: true, so later build/diff/publish runs keep matching what was scaffolded. [default: False]

options.name: --schemas
options.description: Scaffold only these schemas, as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. A schema not named is left out, and 'public' is only included if it is named. Cannot be combined with --exclude-schemas. A name the database lacks is an error. The generated pgproj.json lists the schemas it modeled. A name is folded to lower case unless it is in double quotes, as pg_dump -n does.

options.name: --exclude-schemas
options.description: Scaffold every schema except these, as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. Cannot be combined with --schemas. The generated pgproj.json lists the schemas it modeled. A name is folded to lower case unless it is in double quotes, as pg_dump -n does.

options.name: --report
options.description: Also write init-report-<yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss>.md (the time in UTC) at the root of --output: the arguments used, a summary, every object modeled with its file, what was not modeled (not supported, or excluded), and what is cluster-wide. [default: False]

options.name: --tenant-prefix
options.description: Scaffold a database with a schema per tenant (G-290): the schemas named <prefix>_... are tenants. One of them becomes the template (the Tenant folder, written without its schema name), the others are compared with it and those that differ are named, the shared schemas are scaffolded as usual, and pgproj.json gets a "tenants" block. Folded to lower case unless in double quotes.

options.name: --tenant-from
options.description: With --tenant-prefix: the tenant (its identifier, acme for tenant_acme) to scaffold the template from. Defaults to the first tenant by name.

options.name: --tenant-file
options.description: With --tenant-prefix: also write tenants.csv beside pgproj.json, listing the tenants found, and point pgproj.json's "tenants" at it, so the tenants are that list from now on (pgproj creates a listed tenant's schema). Not with --tenant-query. [default: False]

options.name: --tenant-query
options.description: With --tenant-prefix: write this query into pgproj.json's "tenants", so the tenants are the identifiers it returns from now on (pgproj creates a returned tenant's schema). Not run by init. Not with --tenant-file.

options.name: --erd
options.description: Also write an entity relationship diagram of the project's tables as Mermaid, built from the project's SQL files (not from a database): a bare .mmd file, and for build, diff, and publish a companion .md file of the same name that links and shows it. The optional value is the file's path, relative to the directory of pgproj.json unless absolute; a .mmd or .md extension is replaced, any other is kept and .mmd is added. Without a value the file is erd-<yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss>.mmd (the time in UTC) in the directory of pgproj.json. Nothing is written if the project has errors. The diagram comes from the project, not a database, so publish --dry-run writes it too.

options.name: --erd-schemas
options.description: With --erd, draw only the tables in these schemas, as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. A foreign key from a drawn table to a table in a schema left out is drawn to a stub marked (external). 'public' is only drawn if it is named. A name the project has no table in is an error. Cannot be combined with --erd-exclude-schemas. A name is folded to lower case unless it is in double quotes, as pg_dump -n does.

options.name: --erd-exclude-schemas
options.description: With --erd, draw every table except those in these schemas, in the same list format. Cannot be combined with --erd-schemas.

options.name: --erd-existing
options.description: With --erd, what to do when a file is already at the path: 'overwrite' replaces it; 'backup' renames it to name.<UTC time>.ext first and writes the new one at the path; 'keep' leaves it and writes the new one to name.<UTC time>.ext. The .mmd and its .md are handled together. Without this option a file an earlier --erd wrote is backed up, and a file that was not written by --erd is kept.

options.name: --erd-html
options.description: With --erd, also write a web page (a .html file of the same path and base name) that draws the diagram in a browser. The page loads Mermaid from a CDN, so it needs internet access to draw. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Also write what the command is doing (each file read, the server version, the time each step took, the counts) to standard error, prefixed '[verbose]'. Secrets in the text are masked. Cannot be combined with --quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Write only the command's result and its errors: no progress lines, no warnings, no notices. Errors, refusals, and the exit code are unchanged. Cannot be combined with --verbose. [default: False]

commands.name: build
commands.description:
Parse the SQL files referenced by a pgproj.json project, build the semantic model, and print any diagnostics (errors and warnings) discovered while parsing.

The command exits with code 0 when the model has no errors, or 1 when errors are found.

With --source-connection, a live database is built in place of the project's SQL files: it is scaffolded as init does (in a read-only transaction), so --dump-model and --erd describe the database, and the diagnostics say whether what init would write builds. Only the option on the command line turns the mode on (a bare option reads PGPROJ_SOURCE_CONNECTION); pgproj.json is optional and still supplies schemas, searchPath, and the exclude options; not for a project with tenants. build never connects to a target.

A project with tenants ("tenants" in pgproj.json: a template folder every tenant's schema holds, and the prefix of their schema names) has its template read once, in the stand-in schema (the prefix), and checked: a template statement that creates something in a shared schema, writes a schema on the tenant's own objects, refers to one tenant's schema, or holds something that belongs to the whole database is an error, and so is a shared statement that reaches into a tenant. A CSV file of tenants is read and each bad line reported. See docs/notes/tenants.md.

Diagram:
  - --erd also writes an entity relationship diagram of the project's tables (Mermaid, from the SQL files): erd-<time>.mmd and a companion erd-<time>.md in the directory of pgproj.json, or the path given after --erd. Nothing is written if the project has errors.
  - --erd-schemas/--erd-exclude-schemas (not both) narrow the diagram to some schemas; a foreign key out of them is drawn to an (external) stub.
  - --erd-html also writes a web page (erd-<time>.html) that draws the diagram in a browser; it loads Mermaid from a CDN.
  - --erd-existing overwrite|backup|keep says what to do with a file already at the path; by default a file --erd wrote is backed up to name.<UTC time>.ext and any other file is kept.

--format json writes the result as one JSON document on standard output, the envelope diff --format json starts with: schemaVersion, status (succeeded, failed, projectNotFound, projectInvalid, and with --source-connection refused or connectionFailed), the project, the documents read, the diagnostics, each with its file, line, column, endLine, and endColumn when known, the counts by severity, and with --source-connection the source database. The header, the diagnostics' text, and every other line go to standard error. The exit code is the same.

--verbose also writes each file read and the time taken to standard error; --quiet writes only the errors (to standard error). The exit code is the same either way.

Examples:
  pgproj build
  pgproj build --project ./db/pgproj.json
  pgproj build --dump-model ./model.json
  pgproj build --format json
  pgproj build --quiet
  pgproj build --verbose
  pgproj build --erd
  pgproj build --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --dump-model ./model.json
  pgproj build --erd docs/model
  pgproj build --erd docs/model --erd-html --erd-existing overwrite

commands.name: diff
commands.description:
Parse the project's SQL files, build the semantic model, connect to a live PostgreSQL database, and report the differences between them: each added, removed, and modified object (a modified one with the properties that changed, old -> new, named as they are written: Default, Query, Columns changed), then the counts.

The database to compare with comes from --target-connection, the PGPROJ_TARGET_CONNECTION environment variable, or the targetConnectionString property in pgproj.json, in that order; one of them is required.

With --source-connection, a live database is the desired state in place of the project's SQL files (environment promotion, dev -> QA -> prod, and parity checks): the target is compared with the source, so + is in the source only, - in the target only, and ~ in both with a difference. The first output line says "Source A -> Target B". The source is read in a read-only transaction and must not be the target; the project's schemas, searchPath, exclude options, and pre/post-deploy scripts still apply, and pgproj.json may be absent. Not for a project with tenants. Use --exit-code and --format json for a parity check between two databases.

--exclude-grants/--exclude-role-memberships/--exclude-owners override pgproj.json's excludeGrants/excludeRoleMemberships/excludeOwners for this run, in either direction.

--format json writes the comparison as one JSON document on standard output, for CI: schemaVersion, status, the project, the documents read, the diagnostics with their places, the added, removed, and modified objects, and the counts. When nothing could be compared (the project has errors, the run is refused, a database cannot be reached), the document has that status, the message, and what was read, and the exit code is 1.

A project with tenants ("tenants" in pgproj.json, a schema per tenant built from one template) is compared in parts: the shared schemas once, then each tenant's schema against the template. The tenants are grouped by the changes they need, shown once in the template's stand-in schema (the prefix); a tenant whose schema does not exist yet is counted, and tenants with nothing to change are named. A schema named as a tenant's that the tenant query or file no longer lists is left as it is, and a warning says to drop it by other means. --tenants a,b compares only those tenants. The closing counts add up every tenant. See docs/notes/tenants.md.

Exit codes: 0 when diff ran (whatever it found), 1 on an error (no connection, a project with errors). With --exit-code: 0 when there are no differences, 2 when there are, 1 on an error; warnings do not count as differences.

Diagram:
  - --erd also writes an entity relationship diagram of the project's tables (Mermaid, from the SQL files, not the database): erd-<time>.mmd and a companion erd-<time>.md in the directory of pgproj.json, or the path given after --erd. It is written before the database is read.
  - --erd-schemas/--erd-exclude-schemas (not both) narrow the diagram to some schemas; a foreign key out of them is drawn to an (external) stub.
  - --erd-html also writes a web page (erd-<time>.html) that draws the diagram in a browser; it loads Mermaid from a CDN.
  - --erd-existing overwrite|backup|keep says what to do with a file already at the path; by default a file --erd wrote is backed up to name.<UTC time>.ext and any other file is kept.

--verbose also writes each step and its time to standard error; --quiet leaves out the progress lines and notices, so only the change list (or JSON) and any errors are written.

When the change drops, renames, or retypes something the body of a PL/pgSQL routine names (a table or view, a function or procedure, a qualified column), a warning says which routine names what: PostgreSQL records no dependency for such a body, so nothing stops the change and the routine fails when it runs. The script and its order are unchanged.

Examples:
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=postgres"
  pgproj diff --project ./db/pgproj.json --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app"
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --exclude-grants
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --format json
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --exit-code
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --quiet
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --verbose
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --erd
  pgproj diff --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --tenants acme,globex
  pgproj diff --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=qa" --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=prod" --exit-code --exclude-owners

commands.name: publish
commands.description:
Parse the project's SQL files, build the semantic model, diff it against a live PostgreSQL database, and generate a deployment script that brings the database up to date.

The database to update comes from --target-connection, the PGPROJ_TARGET_CONNECTION environment variable, or the targetConnectionString property in pgproj.json, in that order; one of them is required.

With --source-connection, a live database is the desired state in place of the project's SQL files (environment promotion, dev -> QA -> prod): the target is changed to match the source. The first output line says "Source A -> Target B". The source is read in a read-only transaction and must not be the target; every check (destructive changes, locks, superuser statements, roles, tablespaces, server version) runs against the target, and what exists only in the target is dropped as in any publish (with --allow-destructive). The project's schemas, searchPath, exclude options (use --exclude-owners and --exclude-grants when environments differ), and pre/post-deploy scripts still apply, the scripts running against the target; pgproj.json may be absent. Not for a project with tenants.

A project with tenants ("tenants" in pgproj.json, a schema per tenant built from one template) is published in parts: the shared changes in one transaction, with the pre- and post-deploy scripts, then each tenant in a transaction of its own, its script starting with SET search_path TO the tenant's schema. A tenant the tenant query or file lists whose schema does not exist yet has it created. Every part is checked before anything runs; a failure stops the run, says what was published, which part failed (rolled back), and what was not started, and publishing again finishes. A schema the query or file no longer lists is never dropped: a warning says to drop it by other means. --tenants a,b publishes only those tenants. A tenant's own scripts (tenants.predeploy and tenants.postdeploy) run in its transaction, around the template's changes, with :"tenant_schema", :'tenant_schema', and :'tenant_id' filled in; a file starting with -- pgproj: run when=tenant-changed or when=tenant-created runs only then, and a file of the project's own scripts marked when=changed only when there are changes. A printed or written script has a line before each tenant's part. See docs/notes/tenants.md.

Printing, saving, or running the script:
  - By default the script is printed to the console. Use --output to save it to a file, and --execute to run it directly against the database (use --dry-run to preview without running it).
  - --execute runs the script in a single transaction; a script that is printed or written is not wrapped in one (a warning says so), so run it inside a transaction yourself (psql --single-transaction -f <file>).
  - --execute refuses to run a script that can discard data unless --allow-destructive is also given.
  - Before anything runs, a warning names each change that rewrites, scans, or blocks writes to a table that already exists (a column type change, SET NOT NULL, a new index or constraint, SET ACCESS METHOD, ...), which on a large table holds its lock for as long as it takes.
  - --lock-timeout <duration> bounds how long each statement waits for a lock: past it, the script is rolled back and the statement named, instead of the publish stalling everything behind it.
  - --concurrently moves the slow part of new indexes and constraints on tables that already exist out of the transaction: after it commits, each index is built with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (on a partitioned table: created ON ONLY the parent, then built on each partition and attached), a changed index is built under a temporary name and swapped in, and each new foreign key or CHECK constraint, added NOT VALID in the transaction, is validated. These statements run one at a time, each on its own; a failed one has what it built dropped, is named with the error, and the next publish --concurrently does the rest. A printed or written script has them after a line that says so; run the part above it in one transaction and the part below it without one.
  - An index PostgreSQL marks INVALID (left by a failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY) is rebuilt: concurrently with --concurrently, in the transaction without it.
  - --execute refuses a script with statements only a superuser can run (an event trigger; ALTER TABLE ... TRIGGER ALL on foreign-key triggers; a LEAKPROOF routine or one in an untrusted language such as c) unless --allow-superuser-statements is also given, and then refuses a connected role that is not a superuser, before running anything. A printed or written script starts with a comment naming them, and a warning says so.
  - --execute refuses a script estimated to need more locks than the server's lock table holds (max_locks_per_transaction * (max_connections + max_prepared_transactions); one transaction keeps every relation it changes locked until it commits) unless --allow-lock-limit is also given; from 80% of it, publish warns, and a printed or written script is only warned about.
  - --execute also refuses, before running anything, a project that names a tablespace or a role the server lacks or uses a feature the server's version lacks, or that changes a collation, a text search dictionary's template, or a configuration's parser that something still uses (it names each one); --dry-run and --output only warn about the first three.

Comments only:
  - --comments-only deploys just the COMMENT ON statements the script would contain, to publish documentation (see documentation.md) without touching the schema; every other change is left for a later publish, and the predeploy and postdeploy scripts are not included.
  - A comment on an object the database does not have yet is skipped: the statement runs in a DO block that reports a warning ("pgproj publish --comments-only skipped a comment") and goes on, so the script also runs under psql. Publish again without --comments-only to create the object and set its comment.
  - It works with --execute, --dry-run, and --output as usual. The checks that guard other changes (--allow-destructive, a missing tablespace or role, a feature the server lacks) do not apply, because nothing else is deployed.

Schemas are never dropped: a schema the database has that the project no longer uses is left in place (its objects are dropped as usual), and a warning names it.

--exclude-grants/--exclude-role-memberships/--exclude-owners override pgproj.json's excludeGrants/excludeRoleMemberships/excludeOwners for this run, in either direction.

Diagram:
  - --erd also writes an entity relationship diagram of the project's tables (Mermaid, from the SQL files, not the database): erd-<time>.mmd and a companion erd-<time>.md in the directory of pgproj.json, or the path given after --erd. It is written before the database is read, so --dry-run writes it too.
  - --erd-schemas/--erd-exclude-schemas (not both) narrow the diagram to some schemas; a foreign key out of them is drawn to an (external) stub.
  - --erd-html also writes a web page (erd-<time>.html) that draws the diagram in a browser; it loads Mermaid from a CDN.
  - --erd-existing overwrite|backup|keep says what to do with a file already at the path; by default a file --erd wrote is backed up to name.<UTC time>.ext and any other file is kept.

--verbose also writes each step and its time to standard error. --quiet leaves out the progress lines and warnings; the script (when it is printed), errors, and refusals are still written.

When the change drops, renames, or retypes something the body of a PL/pgSQL routine names (a table or view, a function or procedure, a qualified column), a warning says which routine names what: PostgreSQL records no dependency for such a body, so nothing stops the change and the routine fails when it runs. The script and its order are unchanged.

Examples:
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=postgres"
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --output ./deploy.sql
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --dry-run
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --allow-destructive
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --exclude-grants
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=postgres" --execute --allow-superuser-statements
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --lock-timeout 5s
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --concurrently --lock-timeout 5s
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --allow-lock-limit
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --comments-only --execute
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --comments-only --output ./comments.sql
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --output ./deploy.sql --quiet
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --dry-run --erd docs/model.mmd
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --dry-run --verbose
  pgproj publish --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app" --execute --tenants acme,globex
  pgproj publish --source-connection "Host=localhost;Database=qa" --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=prod" --dry-run --exclude-owners

options.name: --project
options.description: Path to the pgproj.json project file. Defaults to 'pgproj.json' in the current directory. [default: pgproj.json]

options.name: --target-connection
options.description: PostgreSQL connection string of the database to update. If not given, the PGPROJ_TARGET_CONNECTION environment variable is used, then targetConnectionString from pgproj.json.

options.name: --source-connection
options.description: Use this live database (the source) as the desired state, in place of the project's SQL files: the target is made to match it. The project's pgproj.json still supplies schemas, searchPath, the exclude options, and the pre/post-deploy scripts, which run against the target; the project file may be absent. With no value, the PGPROJ_SOURCE_CONNECTION environment variable is used. Only this option on the command line turns the mode on; the variable alone never does. The source is read in a read-only transaction and must not be the target. Not for a project with tenants.

options.name: --execute
options.description: Execute the generated deployment script against PostgreSQL after it is generated. [default: False]

options.name: --output
options.description: File path to write the generated SQL deployment script to.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the generated deployment script without executing it, even if --execute is set. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-destructive
options.description: Allow --execute to run a script that can discard data or access: a dropped table, column, materialized view, extension, or composite type field; a changed column type that can lose a value (a widening such as varchar(50) to varchar(100) or int to bigint is not one); a cast, operator, aggregate, rule, publication, or event trigger that is dropped and not created again; a revoked grant or role membership; or a changed owner. Without this flag, --execute refuses to run such a script and lists the affected operations. [default: False]

options.name: --comments-only
options.description: Deploy only the COMMENT ON statements of the script (on schemas, tables, columns, constraints, and the other objects that take a comment), and nothing else: no schema changes, no grants or owners, and not the predeploy or postdeploy script. A comment on an object the database does not have yet (a new table, say) is skipped, with a warning that names it. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-superuser-statements
options.description: Allow --execute to run statements that PostgreSQL lets only a superuser run: a created, changed, or dropped event trigger, a table's internal (foreign-key) triggers enabled or disabled (ALTER TABLE ... TRIGGER ALL), and a function or procedure created or replaced LEAKPROOF or in an untrusted language (c, internal, plpython3u, ...). It is consent for this run, not a role switch: without it, --execute refuses such a script even for a superuser and lists the statements; with it, a role that is not a superuser is refused before anything runs. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-lock-limit
options.description: Allow --execute to run a script estimated to need more locks than the server's lock table holds (max_locks_per_transaction * (max_connections + max_prepared_transactions)). The whole script is one transaction, which keeps every relation it creates, alters, or drops locked until it commits, so such a script is likely to fail partway with "out of shared memory" and roll back. Without this flag, --execute refuses it. [default: False]

options.name: --lock-timeout
options.description: Wait at most this long for each lock the script needs (5s, 500ms, 2min): a statement that cannot get its lock in time fails, the whole script is rolled back, and the error names the statement, instead of waiting behind a long transaction and blocking everything that queues behind it. Off unless given. A printed or written script starts with SET lock_timeout.

options.name: --concurrently
options.description: Build new indexes on tables that already exist with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, and check new foreign keys and CHECK constraints after adding them NOT VALID, after the transaction commits and one statement at a time, so they do not block writes to the table while they run. A new unique constraint, or a primary key on columns that are already NOT NULL, is built the same way and added USING INDEX; a changed index is built under a temporary name and swapped in. If one of those statements fails, what it was building is dropped, the error names it, and running publish --concurrently again does the rest. [default: False]

options.name: --tenants
options.description: Publish only these tenants, by identifier (acme, not tenant_acme), as a comma-separated list or the option repeated: to try a change on a few tenants, to finish after a run that stopped, or to set up a new one. Only for a project with tenants; each must be a tenant the project already has. The shared schemas are published either way.

options.name: --exclude-grants
options.description: Exclude object/schema/column privilege grants from the model. Overrides the excludeGrants value from pgproj.json (pass explicitly in either direction). Included by default.

options.name: --exclude-role-memberships
options.description: Exclude role memberships (GRANT role TO grantee) from the model. Overrides the excludeRoleMemberships value from pgproj.json (pass explicitly in either direction). Included by default.

options.name: --exclude-owners
options.description: Exclude object owners (ALTER ... OWNER TO) from the model. Overrides the excludeOwners value from pgproj.json (pass explicitly in either direction). Included by default.

options.name: --erd
options.description: Also write an entity relationship diagram of the project's tables as Mermaid, built from the project's SQL files (not from a database): a bare .mmd file, and for build, diff, and publish a companion .md file of the same name that links and shows it. The optional value is the file's path, relative to the directory of pgproj.json unless absolute; a .mmd or .md extension is replaced, any other is kept and .mmd is added. Without a value the file is erd-<yyyy-MM-dd-HH-mm-ss>.mmd (the time in UTC) in the directory of pgproj.json. Nothing is written if the project has errors. The diagram comes from the project, not a database, so publish --dry-run writes it too.

options.name: --erd-schemas
options.description: With --erd, draw only the tables in these schemas, as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. A foreign key from a drawn table to a table in a schema left out is drawn to a stub marked (external). 'public' is only drawn if it is named. A name the project has no table in is an error. Cannot be combined with --erd-exclude-schemas. A name is folded to lower case unless it is in double quotes, as pg_dump -n does.

options.name: --erd-exclude-schemas
options.description: With --erd, draw every table except those in these schemas, in the same list format. Cannot be combined with --erd-schemas.

options.name: --erd-existing
options.description: With --erd, what to do when a file is already at the path: 'overwrite' replaces it; 'backup' renames it to name.<UTC time>.ext first and writes the new one at the path; 'keep' leaves it and writes the new one to name.<UTC time>.ext. The .mmd and its .md are handled together. Without this option a file an earlier --erd wrote is backed up, and a file that was not written by --erd is kept.

options.name: --erd-html
options.description: With --erd, also write a web page (a .html file of the same path and base name) that draws the diagram in a browser. The page loads Mermaid from a CDN, so it needs internet access to draw. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Also write what the command is doing (each file read, the server version, the time each step took, the counts) to standard error, prefixed '[verbose]'. Secrets in the text are masked. Cannot be combined with --quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Write only the command's result and its errors: no progress lines, no warnings, no notices. Errors, refusals, and the exit code are unchanged. Cannot be combined with --verbose. [default: False]

commands.name: document

options.name: --project
options.description: Path to the pgproj.json project file to document. Defaults to 'pgproj.json' in the current directory. Not read when --source-connection is given. [default: pgproj.json]

options.name: --source-connection
options.description: Document this live PostgreSQL database (the source) instead of the project's files. With no value, the PGPROJ_SOURCE_CONNECTION environment variable is used, then sourceConnectionString from pgproj.json.

options.name: --format
options.description: The formats to write: html, markdown, and json, as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. Defaults to html and json.

options.name: --output
options.description: The directory to write database-documentation.html, .md, and .json to. Relative to the directory of pgproj.json (or to the current directory with --source-connection). Defaults to 'docs'.

options.name: --existing
options.description: What to do when a file is already there: 'overwrite' replaces it; 'backup' renames it to name.<UTC time>.ext first and writes the new one at the path; 'keep' leaves it and writes the new one to name.<UTC time>.ext. All the files are handled together. Without this option a file 'document' wrote is backed up, and a file it did not write is kept.

options.name: --schemas
options.description: Document only these schemas (and draw only their tables), as a comma-separated list or the option repeated. 'public' is only included if it is named. Cannot be combined with --exclude-schemas. A name is folded to lower case unless it is in double quotes, as pg_dump -n does.

options.name: --exclude-schemas
options.description: Document every schema except these, in the same list format. Cannot be combined with --schemas.

options.name: --no-fail-on-doc-errors
options.description: Exit with 0 even when a comment's tags have errors (a date that is not ISO 8601, both retention tags, ...). The files are written and the errors listed either way; by default the exit code is 1 after an error. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Also write what the command is doing (each file read, the server version, the time each step took, the counts) to standard error, prefixed '[verbose]'. Secrets in the text are masked. Cannot be combined with --quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Write only the command's result and its errors: no progress lines, no warnings, no notices. Errors, refusals, and the exit code are unchanged. Cannot be combined with --verbose. [default: False]

commands.name: about
commands.description:
Prints what a bug report needs, in a form safe to paste into an issue:
  - pgproj: its version, how it was installed, the operating system and its architecture, the .NET runtime, and whether PostgreSQL's parser (libpg_query) loads on this machine.
  - The project: the pgproj.json it finds (or that it finds none), its name, source folder and number of SQL files, schemas, search path, deploy scripts, and tenants. The project is read, not built: pgproj build checks it.
  - The target and source databases: where each connection string came from (the option, the environment variable, or pgproj.json, in that order, as the other commands take them), the host, port, database, and user, and, connected to, the server's PostgreSQL version, whether the role is a superuser, and whether it can create temporary objects (without that, diff compares views and defaults as text, which can show changes that are not there).

A database it cannot reach within five seconds, or that refuses the login, is reported with the reason, and about still exits with 0. It only reads: it changes nothing in a database.

No password is ever printed. Host names and paths are; remove them before pasting if they are private.

Examples:
  pgproj about
  pgproj about --project ./db/pgproj.json
  pgproj about --target-connection "Host=localhost;Database=app;Username=postgres"

options.name: --project
options.description: Path to the pgproj.json project file to describe. Defaults to 'pgproj.json' in the current directory. A project that is not there is reported, not an error. [default: pgproj.json]

options.name: --target-connection
options.description: The target database, as diff and publish take it. If not given, the PGPROJ_TARGET_CONNECTION environment variable is used, then targetConnectionString from pgproj.json.

options.name: --source-connection
options.description: The source database, as init and document take it. If not given, the PGPROJ_SOURCE_CONNECTION environment variable is used, then sourceConnectionString from pgproj.json.

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Also write what the command is doing (each file read, the server version, the time each step took, the counts) to standard error, prefixed '[verbose]'. Secrets in the text are masked. Cannot be combined with --quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Write only the command's result and its errors: no progress lines, no warnings, no notices. Errors, refusals, and the exit code are unchanged. Cannot be combined with --verbose. [default: False]
